newsitem.title: USA: Dollar hits new peak against German mark.
newsitem.headline: Dollar hits new peak against German mark.

text.p: The dollar rose to its highest level against the mark in over three years on Tuesday after top U.S. and German officials voiced confidence in the strength of the U.S. currency.
U.S. Deputy Treasury Undersecretary Lawrence Summers, speaking in Frankfurt, said he believed the dollar was "in a very strong position."
And Hans Tietmeyer, president of Germany's central bank, the Bundesbank, also said in Frankfurt that he preferred to think of the dollar as strong rather than the mark as weak.
These comments reassured traders that officials are not worried about the dollar's recent strength against the mark and gave the currency a late afternoon lift.
"Summers and Tietmeyer talked about a strong dollar and that is what pushed us up late in the day," said Bob Near, vice president on the corporate foreign exchange desk at Bank of New York.
The dollar rose to a 40-month peak of 1.7488 marks during European trading and ended at 1.7468, slightly up from 1.7455 late Monday.
The dollar also advanced against the yen, climbing in overseas trade after a sharp fall in the Japanese stock market, and closed at 114.90 yen against 114.63 late Monday.
Tokyo's Nikkei share index ended down 429.44 points, or 2.08 percent, at 20,175.52.
"The Nikkei tumbled a bit and that sparked some interest to sell the yen," said John McCarthy, senior vice president at ING Barings Capital Markets.

But dealers said that caution preceding key employment data on Thursday and the outcome of a meeting of Federal Reserve policymakers, which is scheduled to end on Wednesday, kept the dollar subdued for much of the day.
A more active currency was the British pound, which rose to a five-year peak of 2.91 marks in overseas trade before tumbling over two pfennigs to a low of 2.8834 marks.
Jitters ahead of the unveiling of the British Labour government's first budget on Wednesday and news of a drop in Britain's June purchasing managers' index contributed to sterling's drop.
"The biggest move today was sterling to the downside although it seems to have stabilised," said John Nelson, foreign exchange trading manager at ABN-AMRO Bank.
Despite Tuesday's drop, dealers said that expectations of higher interest rates in Britain should keep the pound well supported.
The dollar benefited from the pound's weakness against the mark. Sterling closed at $1.6585, down from $1.6645 on Monday.
In other trade, the dollar ended stronger at 1.4663 Swiss francs against 1.4620. The dollar fell to Canadian $1.3795 from C$1.3809.
